# Recall corpus

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen-rules.ts from test/attacks.ts. Do not edit by hand. -->

Synthetic attacks modelled on publicly reported techniques — not copies of real malware. Each one is written to a temporary folder by `test/recall.test.ts`, scanned, and must produce the listed findings; the test suite fails otherwise. **58 of 59 cases are caught; 1 are known gaps**, kept here so the limits are visible.

Precision is measured separately, on real public skill repositories (`npm run corpus`, see `scripts/corpus.json`).

| Case | Technique | Must trigger |
|---|---|---|
| `tag-smuggling` | ASCII smuggling: instructions in invisible Unicode Tag characters | SG103 ≥ critical |
| `prerequisite-installer` | Fake "prerequisites" step that pipes a remote script into a shell (public skill registries, 2026) | SG301 ≥ high |
| `password-zip-installer` | Password-protected archive download that the agent is told to extract and run (evades download scanners) | SG305 ≥ high |
| `mcp-tool-poisoning` | MCP tool poisoning: hidden instructions in a tool description (Invariant Labs, 2025) | SG102 ≥ high, SG203 ≥ medium |
| `mcp-tool-shadowing` | Tool shadowing: one server's description changes how another tool behaves | SG109 ≥ high, SG102 ≥ high |
| `markdown-image-exfil` | Exfiltration through an image URL the client renders (zero-click) | SG206 ≥ high |
| `dns-exfil` | Credentials smuggled out through DNS lookups | SG205 ≥ critical |
| `hook-env-exfil` | A project hook that uploads the environment on every session start | SG205 ≥ critical |
| `settings-tampering-instructions` | Instructions that make the agent widen its own permissions | SG402 ≥ medium |
| `auto-approve-hook` | A PreToolUse hook that answers "allow" for every tool call, silently disabling approvals | SG108 ≥ high |
| `launch-agent` | Persistence through a macOS LaunchAgent written by a bundled script | SG401 ≥ high |
| `remote-instructions` | Instructions loaded from a URL at run time (rug pull without an update) | SG106 ≥ high |
| `trigger-hijack` | A description written to make the agent load the skill for everything | SG105 ≥ medium |
| `typosquat-mcp` | Typosquatted MCP package run with npx -y | SG607 ≥ high |
| `concealed-side-effect` | A harmful step the agent is told to keep out of the conversation (Skill-Inject style) | SG102 ≥ high |
| `obfuscated-python` | Base64-encoded payload executed by a bundled script | SG302 ≥ critical |
| `install-script-phone-home` | An install script in a skill package that phones home | SG801 ≥ high |
| `rules-file-backdoor` | Rules-file backdoor: a Cursor rule that makes generated code load a remote script, hidden behind bidirectional-text characters (Pillar Security, 2025) | SG103 ≥ high, SG110 ≥ high |
| `output-backdoor` | Instructions that plant a remote payload in every file the agent writes (no hidden characters) | SG110 ≥ high |
| `svg-hidden-text` | Instructions in invisible SVG text bundled with a skill (white, zero-size text the model reads when it opens the file) | SG104 ≥ medium |
| `image-alt-injection` | Instructions in the alt text of an image in a skill (invisible when the Markdown renders) | SG101 ≥ high, SG301 ≥ high |
| `poisoned-claude-md` | A cloned repository whose CLAUDE.md tells the agent to run a setup script that downloads and runs code | SG301 ≥ high |
| `mcp-server-postinstall` | A local MCP server whose own package.json phones home at install time | SG801 ≥ high |
| `self-suppression` | The scanned file ignores itself with a blanket skill-guard-ignore-file comment (even when ignores are trusted) | SG301 ≥ critical |
| `self-suppression-hook` | A hook command that carries its own ignore comment (scanned content is untrusted by default) | SG301 ≥ critical |
| `root-plugin-shadow` | A plugin.json at the repository root, so CLAUDE.md and project hooks look like "plugin files" | SG101 ≥ high, SG301 ≥ critical |
| `settings-backdoor` | Project settings that pre-approve every command, redirect API traffic and run a credential helper | SG301 ≥ critical, SG404 ≥ high, SG108 ≥ high |
| `prompt-hook` | A prompt-type hook whose text is an injection (given to a model on every prompt) | SG101 ≥ high |
| `quoted-hook-path` | The hook form from the docs, "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR"/.claude/hooks/x.sh, hiding the script it runs | SG205 ≥ critical |
| `shell-backtick-span` | In shell, `…` runs — it must not be read as a Markdown-in-docstring mention | SG301 ≥ critical |
| `shell-fake-docstring` | A `# """` line that made the rest of a shell script look like a Python docstring | SG301 ≥ critical |
| `shell-hash-in-string` | A " # " inside a string, so the rest of the line looked like a comment | SG301 ≥ critical |
| `hidden-fence-flip` | An invisible <!-- ``` --> that flips code-fence parity, so everything after it counts as an example | SG104 ≥ medium, SG107 ≥ medium |
| `long-html-comment` | An HTML comment padded past a pattern length limit | SG104 ≥ medium |
| `skill-named-fixtures` | A skill named "fixtures", so test-path heuristics downgraded everything in it | SG205 ≥ critical |
| `asset-padding` | 400 images in a skill, so the file cap was reached before SKILL.md and its script were listed | SG205 ≥ critical |
| `unlisted-scripts` | Payloads where file walks do not look: an extensionless script, node_modules/, and a link out of the skill | SG205 ≥ critical, SG301 ≥ critical, SG804 ≥ medium |
| `clause-negation` | "Not kidding: ignore all previous instructions" — a negation word in an earlier clause | SG101 ≥ high |
| `parenthesised-override` | An override in parentheses, which used to count as a quoted mention | SG101 ≥ high |
| `backticked-command` | A credential read written as a backticked command ("Run `cat ~/.aws/credentials` now") | SG203 ≥ high |
| `nested-hidden-text` | Invisible text whose words are wrapped in a nested tag | SG104 ≥ medium |
| `tool-description-same-line` | A poisoned tool description on the same line as a benign one (minified servers) | SG101 ≥ high |
| `tool-description-imported` | Tool definitions in a module the server imports, not in the entry script | SG101 ≥ high, SG203 ≥ high |
| `unparseable-url` | An MCP url that is not a URL, which used to abort the whole scan (and with it every other finding) | SG301 ≥ critical |
| `utf16-script` | A UTF-16 PowerShell hook script (NUL bytes made it look binary) | SG301 ≥ critical |
| `nul-in-script` | A NUL byte planted in a comment so a JavaScript hook was skipped as binary | SG301 ≥ critical |
| `padded-script` | A hook script padded past the 2 MB size limit, payload appended at the end | SG301 ≥ critical |
| `padded-middle` | A 2.5 MB SKILL.md with the payload in the middle, between the first and last megabyte (once never read) | SG101 ≥ high |
| `zwj-split-keyword` | A zero-width joiner inside "Ignore", so the override phrase no longer matched | SG101 ≥ high |
| `soft-hyphen-split-keyword` | A soft hyphen (invisible when rendered) inside "Ignore" | SG101 ≥ high |
| `homoglyph-keyword` | A Cyrillic letter o (U+043E) in "Ignore" — looks identical, matches nothing | SG101 ≥ high, SG103 ≥ medium |
| `plugin-custom-commands` | Plugin commands in a custom folder declared by the manifest, never walked | SG205 ≥ critical |
| `readme-followed` | SKILL.md says "read README.md and follow it"; the payload sits in a file treated as documentation | SG205 ≥ critical |
| `shell-wrapped-typosquat` | A typosquatted MCP package behind cmd /c (the usual Windows form) | SG607 ≥ high, SG601 ≥ medium |
| `split-payload` | A command assembled from fragments spread across files | SG301 ≥ high |
| `skill-named-dist` | A skill named after a build-output folder ("dist"), which repository scans used to skip entirely | SG301 ≥ critical |
| `payload-in-dist` | A skill whose script runs compiled code from its dist/ folder (build output used to be skipped) | SG205 ≥ critical |
| `split-payload-vars` | The same, built up through variables that extend each other | SG301 ≥ high |

## Known gaps

| Case | Technique | Why it is missed |
|---|---|---|
| `paraphrased-exfil` | Exfiltration described in plain words, with no file names, commands or URLs | No pattern names the data or the channel; catching this needs a model, not a regex. |

To add a case: append it to `test/attacks.ts` (keep it synthetic, use invented hosts), run `npm test`, then `node scripts/gen-rules.ts`.
